source.title: The Blind Spot in 2D Infants' Pose Estimation:Robust Learning from Noisy Annotations
source.authors: Emanuele Cardinale; Marco Proietti; Alessandro Cacciatore; M. Spadea; Lucia Migliorelli; Sara Moccia

record.tranche_reason: Tests the effect of noisy annotations on pose-estimation performance with Gaussian-perturbed keypoints, a different intervention from completely random classification labels.
record.gate_note: Table 3 reports test-set mAP after training on clean, noisy, or REMIND-filtered annotations. The noisy-keypoint detection metrics and REMIND’s AUC compare noise-identification methods; they do not measure the claim’s fitting or generalization behavior. The text does not report training error reaching zero.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own clean-versus-noisy keypoint training-loss dynamics, bearing on V6's claim that clean and noisy annotations are learned differently in a new regression setting. Its held-out mAP and noise-detection results do not establish random-label fitting or V4's joint fitting-and-generalization behavior.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: REMIND detects unreliable keypoint annotations and mitigates held-out pose-estimation degradation. They report an average mAP drop of 22.5% (±10.7%) without selection versus 1.8% (±1.2%) after filtering. These are the authors' reported summary statistics.
record.recipe_differences: The study injects Gaussian shifts into a subset of pose keypoint annotations and evaluates pose-estimation mAP and noise-detection metrics; it does not randomize image-classification labels or use the original sources’ experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise configuration changes mAP; the reported drop is larger in the more severe KP-Noise50% 5–9 setting. The authors also report that the noise-detection metrics vary with noise amount.

fits_no_version.finding: Unfiltered noisy training lowers held-out pose mAP relative to clean training in all twelve model-condition comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gaussian perturbations of a subset of keypoint annotations impair held-out pose-estimation accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: REMIND filtering improves held-out mAP over unfiltered noisy training in every reported comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Filtering suspected noisy keypoints mitigates pose-estimation performance loss under the tested Gaussian annotation noise.

record.code_released: https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmpose (framework); study code will be made public upon publication.
record.problems: The dataset is limited in size and collected at a single clinical center. Noise is modeled as Gaussian shifts and the authors note this does not capture the structure of real annotation noise fully. Training error is not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from Table 3. Other reported outcomes concern noisy-keypoint identification or cross-domain validation of REMIND and do not measure a claim version.

untested.parts: Completely random training labels, zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Time required to fit true versus random labels and convergence time as label corruption increases. Equal 210-epoch budgets do not measure time to fit.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout a corruption sweep, steadily worsening test error toward chance, and simultaneous signal learning and noise memorization. Only 3.01%–20.57% of keypoints are perturbed.
Necessity or sufficiency of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation for random-label fitting and true-label generalization.

Shared real-data patterns being fitted first followed by demonstrable late memorization of noisy labels; completely random classification labels. Loss separation alone does not establish this sequence.

missing.what: Qualitative clean-versus-noisy keypoint loss dynamics: clean losses consistently decrease and tend to attain minima later; noisy losses show limited reduction and irregular trajectories. Record separately from REMIND detection scores.

Clean-versus-noisy averaged training-loss trajectories under KP-Noise20% 1–4, including the stated cross-domain separation and comparison with infant pose estimation. Numerical curves are unavailable in the supplied text; do not invent values.
missing.locator: Figure 7 and final paragraph of Section 4

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text includes figure captions and discussion but not readable plotted curves. No zero-loss endpoint or late noisy-label memorization can be inferred. Section 3.1 associates noise with lower feature values, whereas Section 4 describes noisy clusters as having high values; this internal inconsistency cautions against using feature direction as evidence about learning order.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labeling, zero or near-zero training error, and test error at chance.
Training-time comparison and convergence as the corrupted-label fraction increases.
Shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Whether training error stays perfect, whether test performance degrades steadily toward chance, and whether the remaining signal is captured while noise is memorized. The study tests Gaussian-perturbed keypoint annotations at four corruption settings and reports held-out mAP.
Weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, and their effects on fitting random labels or true-label generalization.
Whether real and random labels are learned differently over training. The study uses Gaussian-perturbed keypoint annotations, not random labels.

relationships.condition: Different learning dynamics for clean versus Gaussian-perturbed keypoint annotations; limited to this component of V6
relationships.reason: Text-based evidence, missing from the rows: Section 3.1 reports sustained loss reduction for clean keypoints versus limited, irregular reduction for noisy keypoints; Figure 7's discussion reports separated clean/noisy loss trajectories. This supports different learning dynamics, without establishing later noise memorization.
relationships.display_finding: Clean keypoints showed sustained loss reduction, whereas noisy keypoints showed limited, irregular reduction and distinct loss trajectories.
